Expectation1: Provide initial medical care to patients
Situation1: The ambulance driver is conducting a routine check of the first-aid kit to ensure all supplies are present and not expired.
Expectation2: Support individuals or groups in accessing essential services and resources
Situation2: They assist someone who is struggling with paperwork or procedures needed to receive public support.
Story: I was halfway through checking the ambulance’s first-aid kit, making sure every bandage and vial was accounted for, when my phone buzzed. It was Mrs. Lee, the single mother I’d been helping as an advocate. She sounded desperate—her application for housing support had hit another bureaucratic wall, and she needed me to speak with the caseworker right away. I glanced at the half-emptied kit, the checklist in my hand, and the clock ticking toward my next shift. As an ambulance driver, I knew the kit had to be perfect; someone’s life could depend on it. But as an advocate, I’d promised Mrs. Lee I’d help her navigate the system, and she was counting on me. My mind raced, torn between the sterile order of medical supplies and the messy, urgent needs of the people I’d sworn to support. Both roles demanded my full attention, but I couldn’t give it to both at once. My hands trembled as I weighed the consequences, feeling the pressure of two worlds pulling me in opposite directions.
